stimulus.text: Paraphrase: In June 1941, President Franklin D. Roosevelt issued Executive Order 8802. The order banned discrimination in defense industries and in government training programs because of race, creed, color, or national origin. It also created the Fair Employment Practices Committee to receive and investigate complaints. The order came after the labor leader A. Philip Randolph, head of the Brotherhood of Sleeping Car Porters, threatened a large march on Washington to protest discrimination in war jobs.
stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of Executive Order 8802, June 25, 1941. Randolph's threatened March on Washington, planned for July 1941, was called off after the order.

source: original; stimulus paraphrased from Executive Order 8802 (June 25, 1941)

options.misconception: The armed forces stayed segregated until President Truman's order in 1948.

options.text: It ended segregation across the whole South
options.misconception: Segregation in the South continued through the war and after.

options.text: It banned discrimination in defense industries
It created a labor union for Black workers
options.misconception: Randolph's Brotherhood of Sleeping Car Porters already existed.

rationales.A: Background from the books: the military stayed segregated through the war; desegregation came in 1948.
rationales.B: The order covered defense jobs and training, not segregation in southern life.
rationales.C: The order banned discrimination in defense industries and government training programs.
rationales.D: Randolph already led the Brotherhood of Sleeping Car Porters when he threatened the march.
rationales.general:
1. The passage states the order's rule: no discrimination in defense industries or training programs.
2. It names the reason: race, creed, color, or national origin could not bar a worker.
3. It also created a committee to hear complaints from workers.
4. The order reached war jobs, not the armed forces and not southern segregation.
Remember: read what an order covers before judging how far it went.
